skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Create detailed implementation plans with granular, testable tasks before features, refactors, or complex engineering changes.
skill.summary: Create implementation plans with granular TDD tasks for features, refactors, and multi-agent handoffs.

content.value_statement: Complex changes often fail when tasks are vague or too large. This skill turns a feature idea into small TDD tasks with files, steps, and checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates a plan file path using docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md.
Defines required plan headers for goal, architecture, tech stack, and affected files.
Breaks engineering work into 2 to 5 minute tasks with action, files, steps, and verification.
Promotes TDD by requiring failing tests before implementation steps.
Includes an example React Avatar component plan for structure reference.
Offers execution options for subagent-driven or parallel-session work.
limitations: Does not inspect a repository by itself; the assistant must gather code context separately.
Does not execute the generated plan or modify project files.
Does not choose project-specific test commands unless they are provided or discovered.
Assumes engineering work can be decomposed into small verifiable tasks.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into small tasks with affected files, test steps, and verification checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Refactor
use_cases.description: Map a complex refactor into sequenced tasks that preserve behavior and keep tests focused.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent Work
use_cases.description: Create a handoff plan that separates tasks for current-session or parallel-session execution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants a clear first plan for one feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to create an implementation plan for [feature]. Include affected files, TDD tasks, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs to change existing code without losing behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to plan a refactor of [area]. Keep tasks small, test first, and identify files that need changes.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Several agents or sessions will share one implementation effort.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to split [project] into independent tasks for multiple agents. Include sequencing, dependencies, and verification for each task.

prompt_templates.title: Plan From Repository Context
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user wants the plan grounded in real code context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the relevant files for [change], then use the writing-plans skill to write a plan under docs/plans with granular TDD tasks and execution options.

output_examples.input: Add a user avatar component with fallback initials.
output_examples.output: A structured plan with a goal, architecture notes, affected files, and small test-first tasks for the avatar component.

output_examples.input: Refactor authentication validation across several modules.
output_examples.output: A sequenced refactor plan that lists impacted files, preserves behavior, and includes verification checks for each task.

output_examples.input: Prepare a project for execution by multiple agents.
output_examples.output: A handoff plan with independent tasks, clear dependencies, and execution options for current-session or parallel-session work.

best_practices: Gather repository context before asking for the plan.
Keep each task small enough to verify in a few minutes.
Include explicit test and verification steps for every task.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad plans without naming the target feature or refactor.
Do not combine many unrelated changes into one task.
Do not skip tests when the change affects behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill implement the plan?
faq.answer: No. It writes a plan and offers execution options, but implementation happens in a later step.

faq.question: Where should generated plans be saved?
faq.answer: The skill directs plans to docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md.

faq.question: Can it help with refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It is intended for complex refactoring when work spans multiple files or components.

faq.question: Does it require test-driven development?
faq.answer: The skill strongly favors TDD and asks for failing tests before implementation steps.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run external commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown planning guide and does not include executable scripts or shell commands.
